title: Policy Preview Notebook — Scenario-driven Routing Editor (Console)
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Build a 'Policy Preview Notebook' experience inside Console: a scenario-driven editor where customers can author routing policies (region selection, tier routing, fallback model variants) and immediately validate them against replayed traffic, synthetic scenarios, and cost/latency estimates. Goals: 1) give operators confidence in new policies before rollout via deterministic previews and explainable diffs; 2) surface cost/latency trade-offs per-route when choosing model variants or tier priorities; 3) integrate safety and guardrail checks to prevent unsafe fallthroughs. Core flows: author policy -> run previews (live traffic replay + synthetic cases) -> examine per-scenario decisions and metrics -> save policy or create canary rollout. Acceptance criteria: - Editor supports region rules, tier prioritization, percentage-based splits, and fallback chains with model variant selection. - Preview runner can replay up to 1000 recent requests (sampled) with aggregated latency/cost estimates and per-request decision trace. - Console shows a scenario diff: expected vs new routing decisions, with explainable reasons and risk flags. - Safety linter warns on high-churn fallbacks, cross-region data residency breaches, and overly-broad catch-all rules. - Exportable JSON policy and a one-click create-canary action wired to rollouts. Non-goals: full autoscaling controls and long-term telemetry retention (these are separate Dedicated workstreams). Technical constraints: preview runner should be a read-only simulation that does not consume production capacity; use locally cached model profiles (latency/cost) from catalog service; reuse existing routing evaluator libraries from ENG-8421. UX constraints: keep the notebook lightweight (no heavy JS bundles), support keyboard-driven edits and quick scenario presets (latency spike, region outage, model degradation).
comments: 2025-02-15 — Kickoff with PM, Design, and Eng. Agreed on 'notebook' metaphor after UX alternatives (wizard, visual canvas) were reviewed. Design to produce 3 mid-fidelity flows by 2025-02-22. ENG to scope preview runner: replay path + synthetic engine.

2025-02-20 — Design shipped initial mocks (https://drive.google.com/mockups/policy-notebook-v1). Feedback from Security: must flag any policy that routes EU traffic outside EU — added as a mandatory lint rule.

2025-02-24 — ENG spike: estimated 5 points. Proof-of-concept routing evaluator completed by ENG-8605; preliminary run of 200 sampled requests for demo. Found gap: model catalog latency profiles missing p95 for some custom quantized variants (ENG-8421 assigned to fill).
2025-02-26 — PM review: added acceptance criteria for canary creation flow and export. UX note: show cost delta per 10k requests and include toggles to view CPU/GPU cost vs token cost.

2025-02-28 — Design critique: prefer a split-pane notebook (policy editor on left, scenario runner + timeline on right). Accessibility check: ensure colorblind-safe risk indicators. Action: DES-412 to iterate.

2025-03-01 — Sync with Legal & Compliance: VPC/private deployments require explicit residency checkbox to enable cross-region fallbacks. Documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood-inference.com/display/Routing/Policy+Preview+Notebook+Spec

2025-03-02 — Implementation notes from ENG: preview runner will run in sandboxed job that reads routing rules and simulated request stream; results persisted to ephemeral preview_id and viewable for 24 hours. Need an API endpoint: POST /console/v1/policy_preview -> returns preview_id; followups: ENG-8605 to create API and ENG-8421 to supply model profiles.

PRs / artifacts: Design mocks: https://drive.google.com/mockups/policy-notebook-v2, Spec doc: https://confluence.redwood-inference.com/display/Routing/Policy+Preview+Notebook+Spec, Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/482

Open risks: - Sampling bias in replay could hide edge cases; plan to add 'targeted replay' where user can filter by customer ID or route pattern. - Performance: running 1k-request replays for many users could become expensive; we will throttle and quota previews per org. - UX complexity: balancing powerful scenarios vs simplicity — plan two modes: Quick Preview (preset scenarios) and Advanced Notebook (custom synthetic inputs).
